paragraphs: We need, first, to summarize the principles of the [opposing] schools in a brief, condensed statement; for once we have done that, the soundness of what we say about what the seeker (al-mustarshid) must hold to will become evident. We say: all mankind, at the most basic level, are divided into two schools. The first school: a group that has feigned ignorance and denied the realities of things, and have not affirmed any knowledge with certainty — these are the Sophists (al-sūfisṭāʾiyya).[{2}] The second school: the affirmation of the realities, of ʿulūm and maʿārif (knowledges and apprehensions) — and this is what all mankind hold, except the Sophists. Now: whoever is a seeker (mustarshid) and wishes to grasp the firm handle (al-ʿurwa al-wuthqā),[{3}] it is not permitted to him to hold the denial of the realities; for if he holds the denial of realities and then the realities are confirmed, he is destroyed — whereas if he holds the affirmation of realities and that turns out not to be the case, it does not harm him. Moreover, the statement of denial is self-impossible and self-contradictory: I mean, the belief that "there is no reality" — for everyone who claims this has thereby affirmed some reality to his own claim; and his statement "there is no reality" is therefore self-contradictory. And similarly: whoever claims that "there is no knowledge" has thereby affirmed some knowledge, since he has himself "known" and "established as true with himself" that there is no knowledge.[{4}]

Among those who affirm the realities, there is then a second division into two factions: one denies the Maker (al-Ṣāniʿ) and does not affirm Him — these are the Dahriyya, the muʿaṭṭila[{5}] — and one affirms Him; this latter is the majority of mankind on whom one relies. So: whoever wishes the wathīqa (the secure ground), it is not permitted to him to hold the belief that there is no Originator and no Maker. For if he believes in His non-existence and then the Maker is confirmed — he is destroyed and doomed; and if he believes in the Maker and then that turns out not to be the case — there is no harm to him in what he believed. This is one of the questions raised by the Monotheists (al-muwaḥḥidūn) against the Dahriyya: they said to them — "If what we say is true (and it is true), then there is bliss for us and woe to you; and if what we say is not true (and it is) — well, then we and you are at parity, since you have no reward and we no harm. For if our position is confirmed and yours falsified, our recompense is bliss and the recompense of our opponents is painful punishment; and if your position is confirmed [and ours falsified], no one opposing you has anything to fear."[{6}] Likewise the path of one who affirms the Creator (mighty and exalted) but who also affirms that the world is eternal alongside Him — his path is the path of one who denies [the Maker], for he is not outside [the same logical situation]. […][{7}] As to the manifest [features of the calendar]: as for [the Sabbath], that it falls on Sunday[{8}] — that he must adopt. As for the rest of the festivals and the new moons: they are, by all our adherents, known by the moon — and with the manifest text of Scripture also, and with the very acknowledgement of the Rabbanites themselves that the ancients used to determine these matters by sighting — until other than that [i.e. the calendrical reckoning the Rabbanites later instituted] — which they have themselves made up. Everyone knows this. So adopting the older sighting-based practice is more proper, until the seeker pursues baḥth and naẓar to its fullness. This, then, is what one may say among us in this matter; and it is plain.[{9}] ---
